The meter also included promises that had advanced, such as a new TikTok venture with U.S. investors, and others blocked by Congress or courts. The articles offer examples of public statements and the administration’s messaging after criticism. After the records were reported missing, congressional Democrats called for an accounting and said they would investigate the department’s disclosure. The report does not show that Trump directed the records’ handling.

The existence of the records had first been reported by independent journalist Roger Sollenberger and was subsequently confirmed by NPR. The disclosure dispute prompted congressional Democrats to seek an explanation; Representative Robert Garcia wrote to Attorney General Pam Bondi demanding a full accounting of why the files had been withheld.
